sentences.text: Henry II -LRB- Henri II 31 March 1519 -- 10 July 1559 -RRB- was a monarch of the House of Valois who ruled as King of France from 31 March 1547 until his death in 1559 .	King of France	List of French monarchs	House of Valois	House of Valois

The second son of Francis I , he became Dauphin of France upon the death of his elder brother Francis III , Duke of Brittany , in 1536 .	Francis I	Francis I of France	Dauphin of France	Dauphin of France
As a child , Henry and his elder brother spent over four years in captivity in Spain as hostages in exchange for their father .	Spain	Spanish Empire
Henry pursued his father 's policies in matter of arts , wars and religion .

He persevered in the Italian Wars against the House of Habsburg and tried to suppress the Protestant Reformation , even as the Huguenot numbers were increasing drastically in France during his reign .	Italian Wars	Italian Wars	House of Habsburg	House of Habsburg	Protestant Reformation	Protestant Reformation	Huguenot	Huguenot

The Treaty of Cateau-Cambrésis -LRB- 1559 -RRB- , which put an end to the Italian Wars , had mixed results : France renounced its claims to territories in Italy , but gained certain other territories , including the Pale of Calais and the Three Bishoprics .	Italian Wars	Italian Wars	Treaty of Cateau-Cambrésis	Treaty of Cateau-Cambrésis	Pale of Calais	Pale of Calais	Three Bishoprics	Three Bishoprics

France failed to change the balance of power in Europe , as Spain remained the sole dominant power , but it did benefit from the division of the holdings of its ruler , Charles V , and from the weakening of the Holy Roman Empire , which Charles also ruled .	balance of power	balance of power (international relations)	Spain	Spanish Empire	Charles V	Charles V, Holy Roman Emperor	Holy Roman Empire	Holy Roman Empire

Henry suffered an untimely death in a jousting tournament held to celebrate the Peace of Cateau-Cambrésis at the conclusion of the Eighth Italian War .	jousting	jousting	Eighth Italian War	Italian War of 1551–1559

The king 's surgeon , Ambroise Paré , was unable to cure the infected wound inflicted by Gabriel de Montgomery , the captain of his Scottish Guard .	Ambroise Paré	Ambroise Paré	Gabriel de Montgomery	Gabriel, comte de Montgomery	Scottish Guard	Garde Écossaise

He was succeeded in turn by three of his sons , whose ineffective reigns helped to spark the French Wars of Religion between Protestants and Catholics .	French Wars of Religion	French Wars of Religion	Protestants	Protestants	Catholics	Catholics
